The implemented repair and compression procedures provide achievable benchmarks rather than certified upper bounds on receiver-constrained performance, undermining the interpretation of the experimental comparison

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach for Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj; Razane Tajeddine; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ($ε= 0.7$), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.

title: Structured Spectral Compression based Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications for Internet of Things assisted Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Li Ping Qian; Zhehan Chen; Qianru Wang; Qian Wang; Yuan Wu; Xuemin Sherman Shen
abstract: This paper focuses on the Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications based on the Structured Spectral Compression (LB-S2C2). Specifically, the Mel spectral matrix of the speech signal is first encoded at the transmitter side through compressive sensing based on waveform segmentation and data quantization. Then, the Automatic Repeat Request (ARQ) is combined with forward error correction to achieve reliable transmission of speech signals over wireless channels. Thirdly, the received signals are recovered as the speech at the receiver side. Finally, we conduct a series of simulation experiments for the performance evaluation of LB-S2C2. Our simulations reveal that the dictionary matrix used for the speech reconstruction is different from the one used for the high-order matrix sparsification by even only approximately 0.1%, and then the accurate speech recovery fails. It implies that the speech data can be securely transmitted when the dictionary matrix is preserved. More importantly, the LB-S2C2 exhibits a very high privacy protection capability with the average voiceprint similarity to be only 0.3, which is much lower than the 0.8 of the semantic speech communication scheme DeepSC-S, and even lower than the 0.33 of the latest speech communication scheme OFI-OFCNB. In addition, our simulations reveal that the proposed structured speech coding boasts a time complexity of merely O(n), and the proposed speech recovery scheme requires the 12-bit memory storage only, which outperforms the traditional encryption algorithms proposed for speech communications. In comparison with the conventional compression techniques, our spectral compression method renders the coding rate of only 3.9kbps, which is lower than the current lowest speech coding rate of 6.3kbps achieved by G.723.

title: Semantic Communications in the THz Band
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: Semantic and terahertz (THz)-band communications are algorithmic and spectral enablers of future wireless networks. This work investigates deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC) over THz channels. We show that DeepSC models trained solely under additive white Gaussian noise generalize well to the tested THz block- and fast-fading channels when receiver-side compensation is applied. To enable fully data-driven reception, we propose a lightweight neural detector that does not require channel state information (CSI). At 0.3 THz, DeepSC outperforms a throughput-matched traditional coded communication system baseline over 0-12 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achieving more than 50 percentage-point higher Bilingual Evaluation Understudy unigram (BLEU-1) score. The proposed pilot-free detector outperforms minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization with both perfect and imperfect CSI and remains robust to frequency offsets up to 50 MHz, highlighting the resilience of semantic communication to THz channel impairments.

title: Image Semantic Communication with Quadtree Partition-based Coding
authors: Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin
abstract: Deep learning based semantic communication (DeepSC) system has emerged as a promising paradigm for efficient wireless transmission. However, existing image DeepSC methods, frequently encounter challenges in balancing rate-distortion performance and computational complexity, and often exhibit inferior performance compared to traditional schemes, especially on high-resolution datasets. To address these limitations, we propose a novel image DeepSC system, using quadtree partition-based joint semantic-channel coding, named Quad-DeepSC, which maintains low complexity while achieving state-of-the-art transmission performance. Based on maturing learned image compression technologies, we establish a unified DeepSC system design and training pipeline. The proposed Quad-DeepSC integrates quadtree partition-based entropy estimation and feature coding modules with lightweight feature extraction and reconstruction networks to form an end-to-end architecture. During training, all components except the feature coding modules are jointly optimized as a compact learned image codec, Quad-LIC, for source compression tasks. The pretrained Quad-LIC is then embedded into Quad-DeepSC and fine-tuned end-to-end over wireless channels. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Quad-DeepSC is the first DeepSC system to surpass conventional communication systems, which employ VTM for source coding and adopt the optimal MCS index under 3GPP standards for channel coding and digital modulation, in performance across datasets of varying resolutions. Notably, both Quad-DeepSC and Quad-LIC exhibit minimal latency, rendering them well-suited for deployment in real-time wireless communication systems.

title: VQ-VAE Based Digital Semantic Communication with Importance-Aware OFDM Transmission
authors: Ming Lyu; Hao Chen; Dan Wang; Chen Qiu; Guangyin Feng; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) significantly reduces redundant data and improves transmission efficiency by extracting the latent features of information. However, most of the conventional deep learning-based SemCom systems focus on analog transmission and lack in compatibility with practical digital communications. This paper proposes a vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) based digital SemCom system that directly transmits the semantic features and incorporates the importance-aware orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission to enhance the SemCom performance, where the VQ-VAE generates a discrete codebook shared between the transmitter and receiver. At transmitter, the latent semantic features are firstly extracted by VQ-VAE, and then the shared codebook is adopted to match these features, which are subsequently transformed into a discrete version to adapt the digital transmission. To protect the semantic information, an importance-aware OFDM transmission strategy is proposed to allocate the key features near the OFDM reference signals, where the feature importance is derived from the gradient-based method. At the receiver, the features are rematched with the shared codebook to further correct errors. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DeepSC and achieves better reconstruction performance under low SNR region.

title: An intent aware framework for semantic edge intelligence in autonomous 6g UAV and vehicular networks
authors: Salma Begum; Mudassir Khan; G. Suresh Babu; S Raghavi; Sapiah Sakri
abstract: Abstract Autonomous UAV–vehicular communication in 6G environments requires low-latency, context-aware, and scalable edge intelligence beyond conventional data-centric transmission models. This paper proposes SEM-EDGE-X, an intent-aware semantic edge intelligence framework that integrates semantic feature extraction, adaptive edge routing, predictive resource allocation, and multi-agent coordination for dynamic UAV–vehicular networks. The framework incorporates cold-start semantic fusion, uncertainty-aware human-in-the-loop reinforcement, semantic conflict resolution, and trust-driven security mechanisms to improve communication reliability and decision efficiency. SEM-EDGE-X is evaluated using a MATLAB/Python-based simulation environment with SUMO mobility modelling, KITTI and UAVDT datasets, and CNN-based semantic encoding under varying UAV and vehicular densities. Performance is analyzed using latency, semantic accuracy, semantic similarity, energy consumption, throughput, scalability, and SNR robustness metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that SEM-EDGE-X consistently outperforms conventional cloud, MEC, DeepSC, and AI-assisted edge frameworks in highly dynamic 6G communication environments
keywords: DeepSC; semantic transmission; semantic channel coding

title: ParaJSCC: A Parameterized Framework for Reusable Multimodal Joint Source–Channel Coding
authors: Kemi Chen; Mingkai Chen; Youjia Chen; Qian Liu; Wei Gao; Tiesong Zhao
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
abstract: Multimodal signals, such as visual, audio, and tactile data, are increasingly maintained as persistent digital assets in immersive communication systems and digital twins. In these settings, the same multimodal content is repeatedly accessed by heterogeneous receivers with varying modality and bandwidth requirements. Existing compression and Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) methods typically follow a per-request encoding paradigm, resulting in redundant computation and low efficiency during repeated access. To address this issue, we propose ParaJSCC, a multimodal JSCC framework designed for reusable representation serving. ParaJSCC converts each multimodal sample offline at the cloud/content server into a compact, quantized parameter package, which is then stored at the edge serving node for low-latency access. During serving, only the subset required by the current request is transmitted over the wireless channel, followed by lightweight decoding at the receiver. The framework employs a progressive shared-private parameterization to support modality-selective transmission and scalable reconstruction under varying bandwidth constraints. Experiments on multimodal datasets show that ParaJSCC significantly reduces online latency (e.g., from 17.18 ms to 4.34 ms for image-only requests and from 43.96 ms to 11.21 ms for full multimodal requests) and transmission rate (by 47.8%--51.2% for selective requests), while maintaining strong reconstruction quality under noisy channels.

title: QISFP: a quantum-inspired semantic fidelity protocol for energy-efficient and noise-resilient visual IoT transmission
authors: David Elias Emmanuel; Anil Fernando
abstract: Abstract Visual Internet of Things deployments operate under coupled bandwidth, energy and channel-reliability constraints, yet conventional video coding optimises pixel-level reconstruction rather than the preservation of task-relevant meaning. This paper presents QISFP, a quantum-inspired semantic fidelity protocol that treats semantic degradation as a stochastic state transformation rather than as additive signal distortion. It couples delta encoding of temporally associated object-level semantic states with a stochastic channel built from classical analogues of the depolarizing and amplitude-damping maps, and reconstructs meaning by energy- and confidence-weighted fusion over a temporal window. The framework is classical throughout: the quantum formalism supplies trace-preserving maps whose diagonal restriction is a stochastic matrix, which keeps per-object cost linear rather than quadratic in the semantic dimension. The induced class channel is shown to be $$M$$ M -ary symmetric, yielding two independent decay constants that characterise a semantic link and fix a multi-hop relaying budget, while a source-channel separation argument gives the attainability limit $$F \le 1 - p_d(1-1/M)$$ F ≤ 1 - p d ( 1 - 1 / M ) , met with equality by uncoded single-observation transmission; every attainable gain therefore lies in the temporal dimension. Simulation on CDNet 2014 and UCF-101 indicates 27.5% lower energy per frame and 30.3% lower transmitted volume than full-frame x264, with semantic fidelity of 0.922 against 0.855 for a frame-wise semantic baseline, at a cost of 1.28 dB in PSNR. An end-to-end measurement on detector output tests the theory directly: the frame-wise baseline tracks the single-use limit to within 0.022 IoU, the framework exceeds that limit wherever the channel is non-trivial, and at matched fidelity it requires between 42% and 64% fewer bits than the baseline. The protocol requires a few kilobytes of state and fewer than $$10^4$$ 10 4 operations per frame, so embedded feasibility is governed by the choice of semantic extractor rather than by QISFP itself.

title: Adaptive Channel Coding with Semantic-Aware Error Protection for 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Ambar Bajpai
abstract: Abstract Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) — comprising low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, high-altitude platform stations (HAPS), and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) — are increasingly regarded as a foundational layer of sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, extending connectivity to rural, maritime, and disaster-affected regions that remain beyond the economic reach of terrestrial infrastructure. NTN links, however, present a uniquely hostile channel environment: long and time-varying propagation delay, large Doppler shifts induced by high relative platform velocity, deep fades from atmospheric and rain attenuation, and severe constraints on onboard power and computation. Conventional fixed-rate or classically-adaptive channel coding schemes, which react only to instantaneous signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), are poorly matched to this environment: they either over-provision redundancy, wasting scarce bandwidth and energy, or under-provision it and trigger the so-called cliff effect, in which a small SNR drop causes catastrophic decoding failure. In this paper we propose semantic-aware adaptive channel coding (SA-ACC), a framework that couples semantic importance estimation with rate- and redundancy-adaptive coding so that error-protection resources are allocated according to the task-relevant meaning of transmitted content rather than uniformly across all bits. We formalize the system model for a representative NTN scenario — a LEO downlink relayed through a HAPS node — define a semantic importance metric derived from task-gradient sensitivity, and design a two-stage adaptation control loop that jointly selects code rate, modulation order, and per-feature protection level under explicit delay and energy budgets. We further specify a complete evaluation methodology, comparing SA-ACC against fixed-rate LDPC/polar coding, conventional adaptive coding and modulation (ACM), and non-semantic deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) across bit error rate, block error rate, semantic fidelity, throughput, latency, and energy metrics, and use this methodology to reason about SA-ACC’s expected behavior ahead of full numerical validation. Our architectural analysis indicates that SA-ACC should be able to sustain task-relevant reconstruction quality at lower effective SNR than baselines optimized purely at the bit level, at the cost of additional encoder and decoder complexity that we discuss explicitly. We close by outlining the simulation and ablation study required to convert this design-and-methodology contribution into a fully validated result.

title: Leakage-Aware Encrypted Semantic Communication with Key-Conditioned Signal Perturbation
authors: Omar Kaaki; Maria Slim; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Encrypted semantic communication systems protect transmitted messages by inserting key-conditioned modules into a deep-learning semantic communication pipeline, but existing designs rely on a fixed adversarial weight and operate mainly at the semantic-feature level. We propose two changes to the encrypted semantic communication system (ESCS): a key-conditioned signal-domain perturbation layer, called learned adversarial perturbation injection (LAPI), and an information noise-contrastive estimation (InfoNCE)-guided adaptive training rule that {adds an adaptive leakage penalty alongside the fixed adversarial objective} using an InfoNCE-based proxy for mutual information leakage. Experiments on the Europarl corpus over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading channels show that InfoNCE-guided training is the primary source of eavesdropper suppression, reducing the eavesdropper's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) score to approximately 0.07 at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Adding LAPI to the InfoNCE-guided objective further lowers the InfoNCE-estimated leakage by 5-9% with low measured inference overhead, while its impact on legitimate-receiver BLEU depends on channel conditions. The two mechanisms operate on different parts of the pipeline and can be jointly applied.

title: Resource optimization for RIS-UAV integrated air-ground cooperative semantic communication driven by deep reinforcement learning
authors: Yufei Dai; Yuanyuan Yao; Sai Huang; Xinwei Yue
abstract: To meet the 6G semantic transmission requirements, this paper proposes an air-ground dual-mode semantic transmission architecture for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. By dynamically assigning RIS-reflected links to users with long packets and direct UAV line-of-sight (LOS) links to users with short packets, we jointly optimize semantic symbols, RIS phase shifts, UAV three-dimensional (3D) trajectory, and transmit power to maximize the system-level semantic Quality of Experience (QoE). To efficiently solve the formulated non-convex mixed-integer optimization problem, we present an Action Space Decoupled Hybrid Deep Reinforcement Learning (ASD-HDRL) framework, which employs the Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) for discrete semantic resource decision-making and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) for continuous control optimization. Simulation results verify that the proposed ASD-HDRL achieves superior system-level semantic QoE performance.

title: Semantic SCL Decoding for Polar Codes
authors: Andy Huang; Chentao Yue; Branka S. Vucetic; Yonghui Li
abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving communication reliability by exploiting the inherent structure and semantic dependencies of transmitted information. This paper proposes a semantic successive cancellation list (SCL) decoder for polar codes carrying natural-language text. A fine-tuned byte-level language model provides next-byte priors, which are converted into conditional bit costs and incorporated directly into the SCL path metric before each pruning step. This allows the decoder to jointly exploit channel reliability and source structure while retaining the conventional polar coding framework. The language model can also be invoked only for bytes whose channel decisions are unreliable, trading decoding performance for latency. Simulations for length-512 polar codes show substantial block error rate (BLER) improvements over conventional CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) decoding. At rate R=0.75 and list size L=16, the proposed decoder achieves more than 1 dB of gain in BLER compared to CA-SCL with the same L. Moreover, with L=8, it outperforms conventional CA-SCL with L=256 in terms of BLER, while requiring about one quarter of the decoding time of the latter in the evaluated software implementation.

title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
authors: Xiaotian Xu; Zhifeng Tang; Guangchen Wang; Nan Yang; Xiangyun Zhou; Salman Durrani; Yansha Deng
abstract: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.

title: Energy-Efficient Risk-Constrained Adaptive Semantic Communications Under Uncertain Adversarial Threats
authors: Maedeh Fallahreyhani; Paeiz Azmi; Nader Mokari; Mohammad Reza Abedi
abstract: Semantic communication systems based on deep joint source-channel coding can provide task-oriented wireless transmission, but adversarial robustness may require substantial radio and receiver-side defensive-computation energy. This paper develops an energy-efficient, risk-constrained semantic communication framework under source-domain, over-the-air (OTA), and potentially composite adversarial conditions. Long-term total energy, including communication and diffusion-purification energy, is minimized subject to average semantic-loss, trajectory-level tail-risk, and end-to-end latency constraints. A recurrent primal-dual proximal policy optimization controller jointly adapts transmit power, semantic/channel bandwidth ratio, and purification complexity using causal channel observations, semantic confidence, imperfect attack-belief estimates, and recurrent history. A conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraint explicitly limits severe semantic failures. On CIFAR-100, at the unseen source-domain level $ε=12/255$, the proposed controller achieves approximately $61\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy with $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.9}\approx0.36$ while using about $9\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. At the unseen OTA level $Γ_A=-5$ dB, it achieves approximately $52\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy, reduces semantic tail risk by $40\%$, and consumes about $8\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. These results demonstrate energy-efficient semantic defense under partially observable adversarial conditions.

title: Guess and Send: World-Model-Guided Semantic Packet Transmission for Robust Video Perception
authors: Yan Gong; Zheng Chu; Wei Koong Chai; Hari Mohan Pandey; Jiankang Zhang; Jingrui Hou; Miao Zhang; Y. Li; Pei Xiao
abstract: Reliable video perception over bandwidth-constrained wireless links requires transmitting information that the receiver cannot already recover from its evolving scene representation. This paper introduces Guess and Send, a world-model-guided semantic packet transmission framework that prioritizes information according to its contribution to the receiver's perception. A shared feature-space world model predicts the receiver's scene state through affine motion compensation and learned residual displacement, while sender-side verification identifies reusable predictions. An acknowledgment-synchronized receiver twin estimates task-impact scores through two counterfactual evaluations, guiding packet selection and unequal error protection over LDPC-coded wireless channels. A compact 3-bit feature representation increases spatial coverage under stringent bandwidth constraints, while predictive fallback sustains perception during packet outages. Experiments on KITTI-MOTS (KITTI) and VisDrone2019-MOT (VisDrone) under Rayleigh fading and AWGN demonstrate substantial gains in low-SNR conditions. On KITTI at a 4.13% reference bandwidth budget, Guess and Send achieves 47.5% J&F at 0 dB Rayleigh SNR, outperforming H.264 by 11.3 percentage points. Controlled ablations show that world-model prediction contributes up to 8.7 points under Rayleigh fading. Object-detection experiments further demonstrate the transferability of receiver-relative predictive transmission across visual perception tasks. These results establish world-model-guided, receiver-state-aware transmission as an effective approach to robust video perception under severe communication constraints.

title: Semantic Prior-Guided Incomplete Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels
authors: Jiali Chen; Ruitao Pu; Yingke Chen; Dezhong Peng
abstract: Cross-modal retrieval (CMR) aims to bridge the semantic gaps between modalities by learning shared representations. Unfortunately, due to the dynamism and inconsistencies in real-world data acquisition, multimodal datasets frequently encounter severe modality incompleteness. Existing incomplete CMR methods adhere to a label-driven paradigm, relying heavily on categorical annotations as the semantic benchmark. However, label noise is difficult to avoid and often coexists with modality incompleteness. To address this challenge, we propose a novel semantic prior-guided framework for incomplete cross-modal retrieval with noisy labels, termed SPIRN. Specifically, SPIRN uses fixed semantic priors as a consistent reference for robust representation learning, noisy-label handling, and missing-modality completion. Based on this reference, Semantic Priors Guidance (SPG) establishes a stable category-level semantic space, Quality-aware Robust Learning (QRL) dynamically evaluates sample quality to distinguish clean samples from noisy ones and handles noise via reverse learning, Prior-guided Global Label Calibration (PGLC) rectifies corrupted annotations for refined supervision, and Confidence-driven Selective Imputation (CSI) recovers missing modalities from a cross-modal memory bank while filtering unreliable imputations with an increasing threshold. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first framework to jointly tackle the dual challenges of modality incompleteness and label noise in the CMR community. Extensive experiments on four widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPIRN outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods in various scenarios involving both missing modalities and noisy labels.

title: Constructing a Regional Slang Lexicon for Electricity Demands via Soft-Label Bidirectional Anchoring and Active Learning
authors: Rong Chang; Lijing Shi; Zhaoxiang Zang
abstract: Power-grid customer service increasingly relies on community social media, where customers describe outages, billing, and equipment faults in informal regional dialect. Such messages exhibit non-standard morphology, semantic drift, and out-of-vocabulary expressions that make manual lexicon construction costly and degrade conventional NLP tools. We propose a weak-supervision framework constructing a regional slang lexicon from curated dialect anchors and power-domain seed terms. Candidates are generated via Pointwise Mutual Information with soft-label bidirectional anchoring, retaining dialect-anchored terms while recording power-domain relevance as separate metadata, and are scored by combining Sentence-BERT semantic similarity with a jieba-based wordhood measure. Uncertainty-aware active learning with rule-based and retrieval-augmented LLM oracles is applied under three query strategies, and the resulting lexicon is evaluated by a higher-capability LLM calibrated against human expert annotations via Cohen's $κ$. On 11,177 real WeChat messages from Yuxi (Yunnan, China), the framework achieves an evaluator-estimated dialect precision of DP~$=$~1.0 with zero false positives. An ablation shows that soft-label layering retains 751\% more candidates than strict power-gating at identical precision, expanding the candidate pool from 41 to 349 terms. Human calibration ($n=46$) yields $κ_{\text{dialect}}=1.0$ and $κ_{\text{power}}=0.85$. The resulting 25--33-term lexicon, 4--5 of which are power-relevant, provides a preliminary resource for dialect-aware power-grid service NLP.

title: When Music Needs Meaning: Semantic Communication as a Transformative Enabler for the Musical Metaverse
authors: Ali Al Housseini; Jaime Llorca; Cristina Rottondi; Luca Turchet; Tiziano Leidi; Omran Ayoub
abstract: The Musical Metaverse (MM) enables geographically distributed musicians, audiences, sound engineers, and AI agents to interact through synchronized audio, visual, kinematic, and haptic streams, imposing latency, synchronization, bandwidth, and scalability requirements that are difficult to satisfy with conventional bit-level communication. This paper argues that semantic communication, understood here as the transmission of musically meaningful information rather than raw audio-visual-haptic samples, provides a principled communication paradigm for the MM. We define the MM from a communication perspective and derive modality-specific require ments; propose a three-pillar framework for musical semantic communication comprising semantics extraction, semantic-aware orchestration, and cross-modal semantic synchronization; survey representative work across semantic communication, music AI and edge orchestration, identifying the gaps that prevent their integration; and propose a semantic-first reference architecture based on device-side semantic encoders, edge semantic routers, and cross-modal semantic synchronization. The resulting framework positions the MM as a concrete and demanding use case for 6G semantic communication.

title: State-Aware Virtual Patient Simulation for Training Psychiatrists in Challenging Clinical Scenarios
authors: Harsh Mohta; C Chandrahas Reddy; Sunhith Reddy Bojja; Manik Inder Singh Sethi; Vinesh Gupta; Raghuram Bharadwaj Diddigi
abstract: Psychiatrists must be prepared to manage patients exhibiting challenging psychological states, including suicidal ideation, hallucinations, and other high-risk behaviors. However, opportunities to safely practice such interactions are limited. While recent conversational agents can simulate patients, existing approaches largely rely on large language models (LLMs) to determine patient responses, making it difficult to consistently maintain psychological state, adapt to the clinician's responses, and generate clinically plausible challenges that meaningfully test the clinician. We present a state-aware virtual patient simulation pipeline for training psychiatrists in challenging clinical scenarios. The proposed system maintains an evolving patient state throughout the interaction and orchestrates patient behavior rather than leaving response generation entirely to an LLM. At each interaction, a learning-based behavioral strategy selector determines the type and level of challenge appropriate to the current patient and clinician context. The selected strategy, patient state, clinician response, interaction history, and relevant clinical knowledge are then provided as grounded context to an LLM to generate a semantically relevant and psychologically consistent patient response. Following each session, the system analyzes the interaction and provides feedback to the clinician on their communication and management of the virtual patient.

title: SparseLift: Automatically Optimizing Opaque Sparse Paths in Industrial-Scale Recommendation Model Training
authors: Changqing Shi; Anan Liu; Genbao Chen; Junchao Yang
abstract: The sparse path, comprising sparse operations and collective communication, is a critical component of large-scale recommendation models. However, these operations are often represented as opaque nodes in the training computation graph, hindering whole-graph optimization. We present SparseLift, a low-overhead compiler for the sparse path of large-scale recommendation training. It exposes sparse computation and communication to whole-graph analysis to expand the optimization space and improve training efficiency. By analyzing model structure and runtime information, SparseLift reconstructs opaque nodes as analyzable subgraphs, recovering the resource semantics of sparse computation and communication within the graph. Building on the recovered semantics, we design incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to automatically select and organize subgraph optimizations into an execution plan that is reused during subsequent steady-state training. We evaluate SparseLift on an industrial video-platform recommendation task with 100B sparse parameters and the public DLRM benchmark. SparseLift improves steady-state throughput for ordinary industrial training steps by 16.5\% over the native baseline. On DLRM, it achieves $1.60\times$ and $1.26\times$ model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline and TorchRec, respectively.

title: RadPose: ISAC-based RF 3D Human Pose Estimation
authors: Geo Jie Zhou; Kunzhe Song; Ruxin Lin; Huacheng Zeng
abstract: Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Although mmWave radars provide robustness to illumination and occlusion, they rely on dedicated hardware and licensed spectrum, limiting scalability. In this paper, we present RadPose, a learning-based monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that enables mmWave communication devices to perform 3D human pose estimation. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. To address the sparsity and noise of RF observations, RadPose employs a cross-frame transformer-based pose inference network with semantic-guided spatial attention and target-driven temporal attention for robust spatio-temporal aggregation. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Extensive experiments demonstrate RadPose achieves competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art radar-based approaches while maintaining robust performance in unseen and occluded scenarios. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Geo-Chou/RadPose.

title: Designing an Integrated Play Therapy Program Based on the Cognitive-Behavioral Approach and Sensory Integration for Children With Autism
authors: Mehdi Eshraghi; Mansoureh Shahriari Ahmadi; Roya Kuchak Entezar
venue: The Psychological Research in Individuals with Exceptional Needs
abstract: The present study aimed to design an integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. Using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase framework, valid and up-to-date theoretical and empirical evidence was systematically reviewed and coded. A step-by-step framework illustrating the process of structuring and designing the integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism was developed according to Intervention Mapping (IM). The integrated cognitive-behavioral play therapy and sensory integration program was subsequently presented to 10 faculty members from the University of Tehran and experienced therapists working in a university clinic for children with neurodevelopmental disorders who were professionally involved in the field of autism spectrum disorder. They were asked to provide expert feedback on the developed intervention package to facilitate its refinement. Quantitative assessment of the content validity of the integrated play therapy program was conducted using the Content Validity Index (CVI) and Content Validity Ratio (CVR). The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol. The inductive thematic analysis process progressed from 52 initial codes to 22 axial codes, 14 subthemes, and 8 main themes. These eight themes constituted the conceptual pillars of the protocol and integrated the cognitive-behavioral and sensory integration approaches within a spiral, play-based structure, thereby empirically demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed program design. Another finding of the present study was that the integrated program demonstrated satisfactory validity. The CVI calculated for each of the 12 items corresponding to the intervention sessions ranged from .80 to .90, with all values exceeding the accepted threshold of .79. Internal validity was confirmed through member checking and calculation of the CVI. The developed integrated program constitutes a valid intervention for improving sensory responses in children with sensory modulation disorder. Based on the findings, it is recommended that psychologists working with children with special needs use the 12-session integrated protocol developed in this study as a standardized intervention package.

title: Design of Multi-UAV Cooperative Deep Semantic Autoencoders for Communication Networks
authors: Xiaoling Han; Bin Lin; Nan Wu; Tony Q. S. Quek
abstract: Driven by the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks have become increasingly important for executing tasks such as search, rescue, and monitoring. However, under bandwidth-constrained scenarios, UAV networks still face significant challenges in task execution efficiency and intelligent processing capabilities. To address these issues, we propose Multi-UAV Cooperative Deep Semantic Autoencoders (MC-DSA) for communication networks. The architecture comprises one Task UAV (T-UAV) and multiple Support UAVs (S-UAVs), which jointly enhance communication efficiency and data-processing capability via semantic communication and cooperation. Specifically, we introduce a semantic matching and source selection mechanism, enabling the proposed MC-DSA to handle low-quality images while ensuring effective utilization of high-quality images. The T-UAV broadcasts a task query, and each S-UAV computes the semantic similarity between its local image and the query. Communication links are established only when the similarity exceeds a predefined threshold. The training algorithm optimizes network parameters through gradient descent, improving semantic feature extraction accuracy. The testing algorithm evaluates UAV collaboration efficiency and communication quality. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with benchmarks, the proposed MC-DSA improves image semantic segmentation accuracy while maintaining task execution efficiency. As a result, it reduces redundant transmissions and offers an effective solution for multi-UAV communication networks.

title: Design of a Speech Enhancement-Based Deep Semantic Autoencoder for Wireless Communications
authors: Xiaoling Han; Bin Lin; Nan Wu; Tony Q. S. Quek
abstract: Speech communication plays a crucial role in the Internet of Things and autonomous networks. However, traditional communication systems suffer from insufficient semantic extraction and limited noise suppression capability. To address these issues, we propose a Speech enhancement-based Deep Semantic Autoencoder (S-DSA) communication system for wireless communications. It consists of a dual-branch semantic encoder, a channel encoder, a channel decoder, and two semantic decoders, enabling joint source-channel coding for robust transmission. A key novelty lies in an adaptive semantic noise decoupling mechanism that disentangles target speech semantics from noise representations through an interaction module, thus maintaining semantic consistency under low SNR conditions. Furthermore, a joint training strategy optimizes speech reconstruction and noise estimation, while a lightweight testing strategy reduces complexity by disabling the noise-decoding path. The proposed S-DSA enables more effective separation between speech and noise, and yields higher robustness as well as better reconstruction quality. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed S-DSA as a practical solution for next-generation intelligent wireless communications.

title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion
authors: Shunpu Tang; Qianqian Yang
abstract: Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.

title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels
authors: Xu Pei; Bin Wang; Guangxu Zhu; Yi Zhang; Haiyan Fan
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.

title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
authors: Shenghan Luo; Yin Xu; Cixiao Zhang; Yang Wang; Yujie Cao; Zhuoran Xiao; Wenjun Zhang
abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
authors: Yifan Feng; Chentao Yue; Haiyao Yu; Gaoyang Pang; Xinyu Chen; Hao Chang; Branka Vucetic; Yonghui Li
abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.

title: English as a Foreign Language Instructors’ Professional Identity and Professional Development in Higher Education Institutions
authors: Hijjatul Qamariah
venue: SZTE Repository of Dissertations (University of Szeged)
abstract: Teacher Professional identity (TPI) and professional development (PD) are key constructs for the quality of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction in higher education. However, research in non Western contexts often lacks conceptual clarity and methodological depth in explaining how these constructs emerge and interact. Guided by a sociocultural perspective that views identity as socially constructed, negotiated, and shaped through participation in institutional practices, this study examines how Indonesian EFL instructors construct their professional identities and how these identities influence their teaching practice and engagement in professional development. An exploratory sequential mixed methods design was employed. The qualitative phase involved semi structured interviews (N = 10) and ego centered network cards (N = 11) to capture instructors’ lived experiences and the relational influences shaping their identities. Thematic analysis identified five themes: professional identity construction, professional development practices, pedagogical agency, institutional influence, emotional and relational dimensions. These themes informed the development of a survey instrument, which was validated and administered to 161 instructors across diverse higher education institutions. The quantitative phase used correlation analysis to examine associations among validated constructs: teaching practice, pedagogical knowledge, reflective practice, institutional support, and professional development. This was followed by multiple regression analyses to determine the extent to which TPI predicted these outcomes. The results showed strong correlations among all constructs. Multiple regression analysis showed that mentorship emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .473, p < .001), indicating that instructors who receive meaningful guidance and peer support tend to report stronger professional identities. Self directed learning also significantly predicted identity strength (β = .395, p < .001), suggesting that instructors who actively engage in autonomous learning and skill development tend to construct stronger professional identities. Institutional support also contributed significantly (β = .344, p < .001), demonstrating that supportive institutional contexts foster stronger professional identity formation. Teaching experience was not a significant predictor of professional identity (β = .026, p = .336), suggesting the accumulation of teaching experience alone does s not automatically result in a more developed professional identity. Regression analysis further showed that PI significantly predicted teaching practice and engagement in PD, suggesting that identity plays a substantial role in shaping professional behavior rather than merely reflecting accumulated experience. While professional development contributes to identity formation, the findings suggest that identity exerts a stronger influence on instructors’ developmental choices and instructional decisions, pointing to a reciprocal but asymmetrical relationship. This study contributes to the field in three main ways: (1) by offering a contextually grounded conceptualization of EFL instructor identity in Indonesian higher education; (2) by providing a validated measurement instrument that may support future research and policy-related work and (3) by presenting empirical evidence of the important role of identity in shaping teaching practice and sustained professional development. The findings underscore the importance of institutional environments that recognize the dynamic nature of teacher identity and provide meaningful, long term support for professional growth.

title: M 3 ISR: A Multi-Modal Multi-View Benchmark for 3D/4D Gaussian Splatting and Feedforward Compression
authors: Xinhui Liu; Lei Liu; Zhenghao Chen; Lebin Zhou; Wei Wang; Wei Jiang
abstract: High-fidelity free-viewpoint video (FVV) and interactive rendering increasingly rely on explicit Gaussian representations, yet practical deployment remains constrained by representation size, dynamic updates, and computational cost. Existing multi-view video benchmarks provide valuable real-captured content, but they make it difficult to isolate the effects of controlled camera geometry, representation efficiency, and temporal redundancy. We introduce M3ISR, a controlled synthetic benchmark for 3D and 4D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS/4DGS). The benchmark contains 25 scenes from five indoor and outdoor scene groups, two camera/motion configurations, six synchronized 1080p views, and dense ground-truth annotations including RGB, camera parameters, depth, semantic and instance segmentation, and static–dynamic masks. The shared-center camera design intentionally isolates angular view variation and enables controlled evaluation of novel-view synthesis and representation efficiency. We organize M3ISR into five complementary tracks covering 3DGS synthesis, 4DGS synthesis, 4DGS streaming, 3DGS compression, and 4DGS compression. Representative baseline results show small differences in static reconstruction quality but substantial differences in representation storage, while the evaluated streaming methods exhibit substantially higher reported training or reconstruction cost than the corresponding offline dynamic reconstruction baselines. We further define feedforward compression tasks for 3DGS and 4DGS and provide reference rate–distortion formulations and preliminary baseline evaluations. The benchmark is intended as a controlled and complementary testbed for systematic study of Gaussian-based FVV reconstruction, compression, and streaming.

title: Jurema in Northeastern Brazilian Religiosities: Polysemy, Historical Transformations, and Ritual Circulations
authors: Rodrigo de Azeredo Grünewald
venue: International Journal of Latin American Religions
abstract: Abstract This article examines jurema in Northeastern Brazil through the lenses of religiosity, historicity, and polysemy. Rather than treating it merely as a plant or psychoactive beverage, the article approaches jurema as a point of articulation among vegetal materiality, mystical experience, indigeneity, memory, and historical transformation. Because the term can refer simultaneously to a plant, a ritual drink, an entity, a spiritual line, an enchanted city, and a marker of collective identity, the article argues that such multiplicity should not be read as semantic imprecision, but as a constitutive feature of historically situated religious experiences. It further contends that jurema has circulated across distinct religious formations shaped since the colonial period in zones of contact among Indigenous peoples, Black populations, popular Catholicisms, and local healing circuits, while being continuously reworked up to the present. The argument is organized around three axes: the polysemy of jurema and its condition as a plant of power and ritual mediation; the historicity of its uses, with attention to colonial records, missionary repression, and forms of subalternization produced by colonialism; and its centrality among Indigenous peoples of Northeastern Brazil, as well as its later circulation in contexts of catimbó, umbanda, and the so-called jurema sagrada. In conclusion, the article proposes that jurema offers a privileged analytical entry point for thinking about Latin American religions through processes of intercultural mediation, historicity, and ritual circulation.

title: Exploration and Practice of a Teacher–Student–Machine Tripartite Collaborative Teaching Model for the Modern Control Theory Course Empowered by Artificial Intelligence
authors: Tao Liu; Hongqian Lu
abstract: Modern Control Theory is a core course for automation majors. Its knowledge system takes the state-space method as its main thread, characterized by complex mathematical derivations and abstract physical concepts; compounded by the practical constraint of large-class instruction with over one hundred students, the course has long suffered from three structural contradictions: the teaching process is invisible, learning states are unmeasurable, and instructional support is inaccessible. Relying on the “AI+” Classroom Teaching Reform project and guided by the philosophy of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), this study constructs a tripartite collaborative teaching model involving teachers, students, and AI agents. Practice shows that, while firmly maintaining the teacher's leading role in education, the model transforms artificial intelligence into an embeddable, measurable, and iterable teaching element, providing a referable practical sample for the digital-intelligent transformation of engineering courses.

title: Optimal deployment of third-party cybersecurity tools for reducing risk in operational technology environments: A power plant use-case
authors: Giovanni Battista Gaggero; Paola Girdinio; Marchese Mario
abstract: Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity in power plants increasingly relies on third-party monitoring and protection tools, whose effectiveness, cost, and operational impact are often difficult to compare. This paper proposes a framework that minimizes expected annual cybersecurity expenditure and cyberattack-induced production loss. Its methodological contribution is the joint formulation of portfolio selection and marginal investment justification, accounting for overlapping protection benefits and diminishing returns as tools are added. The framework identifies both the preferred tool combination under assumed effectiveness levels and the additional risk reduction required to justify each investment. Simulations on a representative power plant examine how portfolio choices depend on baseline attack probability and disruption costs, and identify break-even conditions for sequential implementation. These outputs support plant-specific investment decisions rather than universal deployment recommendations. Open-source code and a graphical user interface enable practitioners to repeat the analysis using their own technical and economic assumptions.

title: ExQuery: Explicit Structured Query Priors for Temporal 3D Object Detection
authors: Honglin Sun; Yifei Zhang; Junyang Zhang; Kenji Hashimoto
abstract: Sparse query-based 3D detectors commonly encode heterogeneous semantic, geometric, and motion information into unified latent queries, including when explicit 3D anchors are used. We introduce ExQuery, an explicit structured query framework for temporal 3D object detection. Each decoded query is organized into a shared semantic context slice and physical-state-specific slices for center, dimensions, orientation, and velocity. This structure is preserved from prior encoding to branch-specific regression and is reused to reconstruct temporal queries: predicted physical states are transformed by ego motion, classification scores form soft semantic priors, and the reconstructed query is fused with the stored latent instance feature through gated affine modulation. Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show that our method achieves competitive detection performance, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our proposed modules.

title: On the Effectiveness and Limitations of Open-Weight LLMs for Low-Resource Offensive Language Detection in Danish
authors: Elnur Adl Zarabi; Amit Kumar; Adi Singh; Sierra Nelson; Megan Stubbs-Richardson; Taoran Ji
abstract: We study the effectiveness and robustness of open-weight large language models (LLMs) for Danish offensive language detection, an underexplored low-resource task. We evaluate four model families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen) across eleven prompting strategies spanning five design categories, cross-prompt generalization, Danish orthographic variation, and robustness under balanced and naturally imbalanced class distributions. We compare against three BERT-family baselines with distinct pre-training strategies, evaluated via both masked language model prompting and supervised fine-tuning. Even without task-specific fine-tuning, LLMs can surpass all three fine-tuned BERT baselines, and lightweight finetuning yields substantial further gains. No single model or prompt category dominates, underscoring that prompt design interacts with model pre-training in ways that cannot be predicted a priori. Semantically grounded prompts transfer more robustly, while format-constrained patterns consistently fail to generalize. ASCII transliteration of Danish-specific characters (æ, ø, å) generally degrades performance, indicating these characters encode meaningful signal. At the same time, the gap between a balanced test set (best F1 of 0.84) and the corpus's natural class skew (0.62 trained on skewed data, 0.70 trained on balanced data) -- relative drops of 26.2\% and 16.7\% -- shows that class imbalance remains a critical open challenge. Our code and configurations are available at https://github.com/PASHAADC/Danish-LLM-HateSpeech.

title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation
authors: Jiale Xu; Mingshu Ai; Junjie Huang; Tao Jia
abstract: Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and "hub node bias", yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31\% in F1-score, 6.29\% in Accuracy and 5.95\% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding
authors: Ke Xiao; Banghua Yang; Wenbin Guo; Fenqi Rong
abstract: EEG-to-image retrieval commonly aligns neural responses with representations from pretrained vision encoders. However, these representations may underrepresent fine-grained visual details needed to distinguish semantically similar images. To address this limitation, we first investigate the EEG decodability and complementary predictive value of explicit visual attributes, identifying visual cues that capture EEG-relevant information beyond pretrained representations. Building on these findings, we propose AttrEcho, a framework that enriches pretrained visual representations with complementary, spatially aligned visual attributes. Specifically, Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion (RAVF) integrates EEG-relevant local visual attributes with spatially corresponding pretrained features through a learnable signed residual gate. We further employ Feature Token Aggregation (FTA), which learns dimension-specific weights across regions to aggregate refined visual features for contrastive alignment with EEG representations. Experiments on THINGS-EEG demonstrate that AttrEcho achieves 94.8% Top-1 and 99.7% Top-5 accuracy in intra-subject 200-way retrieval, while maintaining 82.1% Top-1 accuracy as the gallery expands to 1,600 images with same-concept distractors. AttrEcho also achieves 25.3% Top-1 and 53.0% Top-5 accuracy in inter-subject retrieval. These results highlight the importance of EEG-relevant visual attributes and spatially aligned fusion for fine-grained EEG-to-image retrieval.

title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
authors: Yunhan Yang; Yunfei Zhao; Zeqiang Lai; Jiachen Xu; Minxiu Wang; Xintong Han; Xiangyu Yue; Xihui Liu; Chunchao Guo
abstract: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

title: Rethinking Latent Reasoning for Generative Recommendation: Beyond Teacher-Generated CoT and Recurrent Hidden-State Feedback
authors: Yiwen Chen; Fuwei Zhang; Zehao Chen; Deqing Wang; Hehan Li; Peizhi Xu; Hanmeng Liu; Shuanglong Li; Xin Pei; Fuzhen Zhuang; Zhao Zhang
abstract: Latent reasoning in generative recommendation faces two practical barriers: constructing teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision is costly, and recurrent hidden-state feedback requires a specialized execution loop. We revisit both the supervision source and the computation interface. A step-level diagnosis measures how recommendation CoT supports next-item prediction and trace coherence. In the analyzed traces, history analysis is the only step with positive mean contributions on both dimensions, while later preference and intent steps have negative mean answer contributions. Guided by this finding, we propose PHiT (Prefilled, History-Informed Thought Tokens), which learns intermediate states from semantic targets extracted directly from observed item histories. PHiT aggregates cached sparse item encodings to construct these targets and supervises the contextual states of distinct vocabulary thought tokens. All thought tokens are supplied together as ordinary input IDs during a single causal prefill, removing the need for recurrent final-state feedback. With supervised fine-tuning alone, PHiT outperforms the compared baselines across four recommendation benchmarks. Controlled ablations support the value of input-matched semantic supervision, while cost measurements show fast target construction with training time comparable to the recommendation-only thought-token baseline.

title: Decoding spatial and semantic information from large-scale visual cortical activity for natural-movie reconstruction
authors: Yukai Huang; Haoyu Albert Wang; Jiawei Zhang; Jialun Ma; Jiayao Ding; Yiran Lin; Xingyu Chen; Ziqi Gao; Yuguo Yu
abstract: Reconstructing natural visual experience from cortical population activity is a central challenge in neural decoding, particularly for calcium imaging, where signals are noisy, temporally filtered, and paired neural-video data are limited. Here we present Ca2REAL (Calcium Activity to Reconstruct Events, Appearance, and Layout), a neural-to-video framework that conditions a pretrained video diffusion model through separate layout and semantic controls derived from calcium activity. Using measured responses from 7,863 V1 neurons in one mouse, Ca2REAL reconstructed held-out natural-movie clips with 81.4% all-pairs stimulus-identification accuracy, with its clearest gains over deterministic baselines in perceptual and semantic measures. We further evaluated the framework in a stimulus-aligned virtual population of 116,705 neurons assembled from encoding-model-predicted responses across 11 independently recorded datasets. Perturbation and ablation analyses showed that reconstruction depends on distributed, stimulus-specific population structure, with layout and semantic pathways providing complementary spatial and identity information. Temporal analyses further showed improved preservation of semantic dynamics across reconstructed clips. These results show that large-scale cortical population activity constrains the spatial, semantic, and temporal structure of natural visual experience, providing a generative framework for high-fidelity neural reconstruction of dynamic visual scenes.

title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Sungwon Moon; Minji Kim; Hyemin Boo; Daeun Song; Jiyoung Lee
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation. We propose \ours, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action. The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations. The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, \ours retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion. Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that \ours achieves up to 1.61 $\times$ speedup and 59.5\% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates.

title: JEPAhead: From Inpainting to Causal Forecasting for Urban Driving
authors: Daniel G. P. Petrini; Davi Pincinato; Fabio Grassiotto; Pedro L. F. Prado; Alexandre F. S. Osorio; Raphael V. Ramos; Felipe Pamboukian
abstract: We fine-tune a pre-trained V-JEPA1 predictor from bidirectional latent inpainting to action-free causal forecasting while keeping the encoder frozen. Using contiguous past observations, horizon-aligned targets, and group-level causal attention, the model forecasts eight future token groups, corresponding to sixteen frames, in one forward pass. On CARLA Town12, it retrieves the correct future among 591 candidates in 69.0% of cases, compared with 55.3% for persistence, with greater gains at longer horizons and on tokens exhibiting greater change. It also outperforms a compact predictor trained from scratch with six times fewer parameters. Semantic analysis indicates driving-relevant information in predicted features: a fixed linear probe trained on real encoder tokens achieves 0.16 mIoU on patches undergoing semantic-class changes, versus 0.13 for persistence. Vehicle-conditioned retrieval improves over persistence by 15 percentage points at the longest horizon. Pixel-space evaluation shows modest L1 gains but little improvement under LPIPS, motivating direct evaluation through latent and semantic measures alongside an oracle reconstruction reference. These findings support further investigation of latent forecasting for driving perception, while downstream utility remains unverified.

title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
authors: Arpit Bahety; Skand Peri; Sriniket Ambatipudi; Chen Xu; Haruki Nishimura; Masha Itkina; Roberto Martín-Martín
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

title: TICK: Text-Informed Contrastive Kernels for Probabilistic Time-Series Retrieval
authors: Rayen Ben Masseoud; Faïcel Chamroukhi
abstract: The coexistence of sensor data and textual knowledge across industrialapplications highlights the need to align natural language withmultivariate time series. This challenge is typically treated as adeterministic task, ignoring the fact that a vague query may matchhundreds of recordings while a precise one matches only a few. We arguethat text-to-time-series retrieval is inherently a probabilisticcross-modal problem and propose TICK, a framework in which each textquery carries a learned uncertainty $\sigma_t$ reflecting how many timeseries are semantically compatible with it. Without supervising $\sigma_t$directly, we find that it tracks query specificity with Spearmancorrelations $\rho \in [-0.88, -0.75]$ on three independent industrialbenchmarks. We further show that coupling the time-series representationto the text query is a necessary condition for this calibration to emerge:without it, $\sigma_t$ collapses to a constant, eliminating the model'sability to adapt its retrieval scope to query specificity. Because$\sigma_t$ sets the retrieval scope of a query, TICK spends a query-dependentcandidate budget instead of a fixed worst-case one, on top of a frozen33M-parameter sentence encoder and a small patch Transformer, with no languagemodel in the inference loop.

title: Funkční přípustkové konstrukce v češtině a francouzštině: kontrastivní korpusová studie
authors: Ondřej Drobník
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: This paper investigates concessive constructions in Czech and French, focusing on so-called functional concessives—expressions where concessive meaning arises not from explicit grammatical markers but from semantic-pragmatic configurations. The theoretical foundation is the “concessive triangle,” a ternary model based on the disruption of expected inference; although premise P holds, the anticipated consequence Q does not follow (non-Q). Adopting a maximalist perspective, the study classifies concessive constructions under three categories: formal, mixed, and functional, the last being central to the analysis. Drawing on data from the InterCorp parallel corpus, the study proposes a typology of functional categories (e.g., contradiction, alternative, totality, irrelevance) and shows how concessivity can be lexically encoded or contextually inferred. The framework of Construction Grammar allows for a unified treatment of form–function pairings across both canonical and peripheral realizations. The results highlight the cross-linguistic diversity of concessive strategies and offer a new descriptive and theoretical model for future contrastive and corpusbased research.
